the majority of the surveyed publications use evolutionary algorithms (EA), genetic algorithms (GA) and genetic programming (GP) as EC techniques, and most of the proposed approaches are evaluated with the help of a few datasets, such as MovieLens, LastFM, Epinions, and Netflix Prize.

the majority of the reviewed papers use evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to solve the RS problem, the most popular datasets used are MovieLens and Jester, the most used evaluation methods are the mean absolute error (MAE) and the root mean squared error (RMSE), the most used baselines are the item-based collaborative filtering (CF) and the user-based CF and the majority of the experiments reported in these papers are not reproducible.

(i) the majority of the papers use evolutionary multi-objective optimization techniques; (ii) there is no clear consensus on the datasets used in these studies; (iii) there is no consensus on the evaluation methods adopted for the experimental part; (iv) most of the papers use the same baseline techniques; and (v) most of the experiments reported in the reviewed studies are not reproducible.
